citations.claim: Energy just before bounce is conserved around 328.6 J
Body rebounds upward with speed ~27.9 after floor contact
First violation: energy jumps to 430.5 J exceeding 368 J bound

explanation: Single ball dropped under g=30 with dt=1/30 and e=1 conserves energy while falling (330 -> ~328.6 J) but gains ~100 J at the floor bounce, rebounding at 27.9 m/s instead of ~25.7 m/s. Likely cause: semi-implicit Euler with large-step/substepped floor contact applies gravity and restitution impulse inconsistently (e.g., positional correction plus impulse, or gravity added inside contact substeps), injecting energy on a stiff elastic impact.
vision_note: The blue ball falls straight down toward the bottom of the arena and makes contact with the floor around step 25. By step 26 it has lifted off the floor again and is moving upward, looking like a clean elastic bounce with no tunneling or penetration visible.
